newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GIB SAYS SARMA SALE TALK "PREMATURE".
newsitem.headline: GIB SAYS SARMA SALE TALK "PREMATURE".

text.p: Belgian retail group GIB said a newspaper report that it was close to a deal on the future of its Sarma textiles stores chain - for which the group had made clear it was seeking a partner - was "premature".

"I can't add more than is in GIB's annual report. This article is totally premature," GIB spokesman Roland Higgins told Reuters. "We have been exploring possibilities for a year, but are nowhere near a decision."

Belgian newspaper La Libre Belgique said, quoting various unnamed sources, that the most likely scenario for Sarma was that GIB would sell a 51 percent stake to a partner and sell some of the "most interesting" store locations. One interested party was rumoured to be an unnamed French group.
Higgins said GIB had already declared openly that it saw partnerships as the future way to success of both the Inno and Sarma chains of the group's speciality retailing division.
"Inno and Sarma require our attention much more than the others in the speciality division. They need partnerships if they are to be successful," he said.
"With just 27 stores for Sarma, what can we do if we can't find an international partner to hook up with?" he added.

The group's 1995 annual report quoted Raymond Vaxelaire, general manager of GIB's speciality retailing, as saying that stagnating and sometimes falling personal consumption levels in Belgium meant "we should focus all our efforts on sectors with strong prospects and eliminate those sectors without a specific future."

Vaxelaire added in the report, published earlier this year, that Sarma's repositioning was running according to plan and that against a background of stagnation in Belgian textiles, market share had been maintained.
GIB shares were up four francs at 1,312 at midsession on Tuesday.
